svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — The tape ran out before the coral did
svg.desc: Pen-and-ink editorial cartoon set underwater off a remote island. A vast colony of rose coral, drawn as overlapping plates with concentric ridges, stretches from the foreground to the horizon. A fictional diver in a wetsuit hovers above it, eyebrows raised behind his mask, holding up an empty tape-measure reel whose tape runs all the way back to a flag marked 0 m, while checking his air gauge. In the distance a second fictional diver holds up a slate reading Still coral! with arrows pointing onward. A sea turtle, a curious grouper, a school of small fish and the underside of a dive boat complete the scene.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
THE TAPE MEASURE RAN OUT BEFORE THE CORAL DID.
Source: ABC News, 11 November 2026 — Divers mapped a rose coral colony more than 1.5 km long off the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.
